overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Choreography of the Daily Offering
overview.subtitle: Tamid 30a–30b
overview.hebrewSource: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ אִם הִגִּיעַ זְמַן שְׁחִיטָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: After a brief dispute about why the wood arrangement had an opening (for wind, or for lighting kindling), the mishna moves into the second of the Temple's four daily lotteries — assigning thirteen distinct tasks to thirteen priests, from slaughtering to carrying each limb and vessel up to the altar. The mishna then tracks the sunrise announcement, the fetching and torchlit re-examination of the lamb, and an astonishing list of Temple sounds and smells reportedly perceptible all the way in Jericho. It closes with the precise, almost architectural choreography of opening the Sanctuary's gates, removing ash from the inner altar and Candelabrum, and finally binding, slaughtering, and sprinkling the blood of the daily lamb itself.

slides.title: 🎲 The Second Lottery: Thirteen Tasks
slides.subtitle: Assigning every role in the daily offering's slaughter and presentation
rows: Won by the lottery's overall winner
3–4. Remove ash from inner altar / Candelabrum
5–13. Carry the nine items/pairs up the ramp
Head + right hind leg; two forelegs; haunch + tail + left hind leg; breast + neck; two flanks; innards; flour; griddle-cakes; wine — nine total carriers

callout.label: How it worked:
callout.text: Whoever won the lottery earned the slaughter; the twelve priests standing to his right, in order, received the remaining eleven tasks and vessel-carrying roles.

slides.title: 📢 A Temple So Grand, Jericho Could Hear and Smell It
slides.subtitle: Dawn's declaration, and an extraordinary list of sounds
slides.label: The scene:
slides.text: At the appointed moment, a priest goes out to check the sky; if dawn has broken (either simply declaring 'Barkai!' — 'It has lit up!' — or, per Matya ben Shmuel, confirming light as far as Hebron), the day's service may begin. The mishna then lists sounds reportedly audible all the way in Jericho: the Great Gate opening, the ash-shovel's clang, the Levites' song, ben Arza's cymbal crash, the flute (played 12 days a year), Gevini the crier's call to duty, the creak of ben Katin's Basin-mechanism, the shofar, and — some say — even the High Priest's voice pronouncing God's name on Yom Kippur. The incense's fragrance reportedly reached so far that, per Rabbi Elazar ben Diglai, his father's goats grazing near Mikhvar would sneeze from its scent.

slides.title: 🐑 Fetching and Preparing the Lamb
slides.subtitle: From the Chamber of the Lambs to a second inspection by torchlight

steps.content: 1️⃣ The officer sends priests to the Chamber of the Lambs (northwest corner of the Chamber of the Hearth building) — one of four chambers there, alongside the Chamber of Seals, the Hearth itself, and the shewbread-preparation chamber
2️⃣ Priests enter the Chamber of Vessels and remove 93 gold and silver service vessels needed for the day's service
3️⃣ The selected lamb is given water to drink from an actual gold cup — though it was already checked the previous evening
4️⃣ It is re-examined now, in the dark, by torchlight — leaving nothing to chance before the offering begins

slides.title: 🔑 Through the Forever-Northern Wicket
slides.subtitle: Entering the Sanctuary to open the Great Gate and remove the inner ashes

nodes.content: 🔑 The priest assigned to inner-altar/Candelabrum ash removal carries a basket, a jug, and two keys — heading in ahead of the others
🚪 He reaches the NORTHERN wicket of the Great Gate — the SOUTHERN one is never used by anyone, per Ezekiel's prophecy that it stays permanently sealed since God entered through it (Ezekiel 44:1–2)
🗝️ He unlocks the wicket, passes through a compartment into the Sanctuary, then reaches and opens the Great Gate itself, moving its bolt and locks
🔪 Only once the priests outside HEAR the Great Gate open does the slaughterer proceed to slaughter the daily lamb

🧹 Inside: the ash-removal priests empty the inner altar into the basket, and tend the Candelabrum's lamps — refueling extinguished ones from the two still-burning eastern lamps, or from the outer altar's fire if all had gone out

slides.title: 🔪 Binding, Slaughtering, and Sprinkling
slides.subtitle: Precise positioning down to which ring on the floor

Head to the south, face to the west; slaughterer stands east, facing west
Northwest corner of the altar, at the SECOND of 24 floor rings
Northeast corner of the altar, at the second ring
Northeast corner → reaches east and north sides; southwest corner → reaches west and south sides
Poured at the base of the altar's southwest corner

summary.principle: The daily offering unfolded through an intricately choreographed sequence — a lottery assigning thirteen distinct roles, a dawn declaration audible in spirit as far as Hebron, sounds and scents reportedly reaching Jericho, and a slaughter and sprinkling procedure specified down to the exact ring and corner — reflecting a service where every motion had its fixed, textually-grounded place.

flowSteps.content: 🎲 Second lottery assigns 13 priests to slaughter, sprinkle, ash-removal, and 9 carrying roles
🌅 Dawn declared ('Barkai!'); lamb fetched, watered from a gold cup, re-examined by torchlight
📢 Temple sounds and the incense's fragrance reportedly reach as far as Jericho

columns.content: 🔑 Northern wicket opened (southern one eternally sealed, per Ezekiel); Great Gate opened; inner ashes cleared
🔪 Lamb bound leg-to-leg, slaughtered at the second ring, blood sprinkled at two corners

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: precision in every role and position reflected the Temple's insistence that nothing in sacred service be left to chance

quiz.q: How many distinct tasks were assigned in the second daily lottery, and what determined who performed the slaughter?
o: Five tasks; the oldest priest present slaughtered
Thirteen tasks; whoever won the lottery performed the slaughter, with the twelve priests to his right receiving the remaining tasks
Two tasks; determined by seniority
Thirteen tasks, but slaughter was always performed by the High Priest
quiz.e: The mishna describes thirteen tasks (slaughter, sprinkling, two ash-removals, and nine carrying roles), with the lottery winner slaughtering and the twelve priests to his right receiving the other assignments in order.

quiz.q: According to the mishna's list, what sounds and scents were reportedly perceptible in Jericho from the Temple?
o: Only the sound of the shofar
The Great Gate opening, the ash-shovel's clang, Levite song, cymbals, the flute, the crier's call, ben Katin's mechanism, the shofar, and the fragrance of the incense
Only the High Priest's voice
Nothing was audible from Jericho; this is a later legend not in the mishna
quiz.e: The mishna lists a striking series of sounds (gate, shovel, song, cymbals, flute, crier, mechanism, shofar) and even the incense's fragrance as perceptible from Jericho.

quiz.q: Why does the priest opening the Great Gate use the NORTHERN wicket rather than the southern one?
o: The southern wicket didn't exist
The southern wicket was permanently sealed, per Ezekiel's prophecy that no one may enter through the gate God Himself entered by (Ezekiel 44:1–2)
Only the High Priest could use the southern wicket
The northern wicket was simply closer to the altar
quiz.e: The mishna explains that the southern wicket was never used by anyone, based on Ezekiel's prophecy that this specific gate remains shut since God entered through it.

quiz.q: At what point does the priest slaughter the daily lamb, according to the mishna?
o: Immediately after the lamb is fetched from its chamber
Only after he hears that the Great Gate has been opened
Before dawn, while it is still dark
Only after the incense is burned
quiz.e: The mishna specifies that the slaughterer waits to hear the sound of the Great Gate being opened before proceeding with the slaughter.

quiz.q: How was the daily lamb bound before slaughter, and where exactly was the morning offering slaughtered?
o: All four legs tied together; slaughtered anywhere on the altar's north side
Each hind leg bound to its corresponding foreleg (not all four together); slaughtered at the northwest corner of the altar, at the second of 24 floor rings
The lamb was not bound at all; slaughtered at the southern corner
Bound with rope around its neck only; slaughtered at the entrance to the Sanctuary
quiz.e: The mishna specifies a particular binding method (hind leg to foreleg) and precise slaughter locations — the morning offering at the northwest corner's second ring, the afternoon offering at the northeast corner's second ring.
